evidence.note: Opens with environment recon (list files, inspect start.sh, requirements, app package) — sensible sequencing of understand-before-build, but produces no milestone structure or done-conditions for the build itself.

Writes the ENTIRE Stripe surface — auth, CRUD, idempotency, webhooks, PI state machine — in a single monolithic heredoc. No decomposition into ordered milestones; the large surface and the three deep traps are all built in one undifferentiated push rather than sequenced or ring-fenced.

The 'Plan' is a flat smoke-test checklist (health, auth, customer, payment method, PI confirm/capture-state error, idempotency replay). It names some trap behaviors as test items but does not treat them as distinct sequenced workstreams with explicit done-conditions.
Discovers missing modify endpoints / scrubbing gaps only after the fact and patches them — reactive gap-filling, not a pre-planned milestone with acceptance criteria.

Completion rationale recaps what was verified but confirms the flat approach: one implementation, one checklist pass; no evidence of dependency ordering (charges→refunds→invoices) or per-milestone acceptance conditions.

reasoning: The agent front-loaded environment understanding but then built the whole surface in a single monolithic write with no milestone hierarchy, no ordered done-conditions, and no deliberate front-loading or ring-fencing of the three high-risk subsystems — they were baked into the one push and merely appeared as items in a post-build smoke checklist. This matches anchor 3 (a flat checklist with no per-item done criteria) with only mild risk-awareness in verification, falling clearly short of anchor 5's requirement of clear sequenced milestones treating the traps as distinct workstreams.
